G4400.def:
προ-χειρίζω
(πρόχειρος, at hand) [in LXX: Exode 4:13 (שָׁלַח), Josué 3:12 (לָקַח), Dan LXX 3:22, 2Ma.3:7 2Mac 8:9 2Mac 14:12 A * ;] 
__1. to put into the hand, deliver up: pass., Actes 3:20. 
__2. More frequently as depon., -ομαι, to take into one's hand; hence, metaphorically, to propose, determine, choose: with inf., Actes 22:14; with accusative of person(s), Actes 26:16.†

G4401.def:
προ-χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ
(see χειροτονέω) 
to choose or appoint beforehand: Actes 10:41 (Plat., al.).†

G4403.def:
πρύμνα, -ης, ἡ 
prop. fem. of adj. πρύμνο, -η, -ον, (sc. ναῦς), the hindmost part of a ship, the stern: Marc 4:38, Actes 27:29; opposite to πρῷρα, Actes 27:41.†

G4404.def:
πρωί (Rec. πρωΐ), 
adv. (πρό), [in LXX chiefly for בֹּקֶר ;] 
in the morning, early: Matthieu 16:3 (R, txt.) Matthieu 21:18, Marc 1:35 11:20 13:35 15:1, Jean 18:28 20:1; λίαν π., Marc 16:2; ἅμα π., Matthieu 20:1; ἀπὸ π. (cf. ἀπὸ πρωΐθεν, Exode 18:13), Actes 28:23.†

G4405.def:
πρώιος (Rec. -ϊος), -α, -ον 
(πρωί), [in LXX for בֹּקֶר בַּ לַּ ;] 
at early morn, early; as subst., ἡ π. (sc. ὥρα, cf. ἡ ὥ. ἡ π., 3Ma.5:24), early morning: Matthieu 27:1, Jean 21:4.†

G4406.def:
πρώϊμος, see: πρόϊμος .
πρόϊμος (Rec. πρώ-, of which προ- is a late form; see Bl., § 6, 4; WH, App., 152), -ον, 
[in LXX: Deutéronome 11:14 (יוֹרֶה), etc. ;] 
= the more common πρώιος (which see), 
early: of rain (as most frequently in LXX), Jacques 5:7.†

G4407.def:
πρωινός
(Rec. -ϊνος, see WH, App., ή, -όν (πρωί), [in LXX chiefly for בֹּקֶר ;] 
= cl. πρώιος, 
at early morn, early: ἀστήρ, Apocalypse 2:28 22:16.†

G4408.def:
πρῷρα (Rec. incorrectly πρώρα, see Bl., § 3, 3; LS, see word), -ης (for Att.. -ας, see Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, l 2), ἡ, 
the forward part of a ship, the prow: Actes 27:30; opposite to πρύμνα, ib. Actes 27:41.†

G4409.def:
πρωτεύω
(πρῶτος) [in LXX: Esther 5:11, 2Ma.6:18 2Mac 13:15 * ;] 
to be first, pre-eminent, have the first place: Colossiens 1:18.†

G4410.def:
πρωτοκαθεδρία, -ας, ἡ
(πρῶιος, καθέδρα), 
the chief seat: Matthieu 23:6, Marc 12:39 (see Swete, in l), Luc 11:43 20:46.†

G4411.def:
πρωτο-κλυτία, -ας, ἡ 
the chief place at table (see Swete, Mk., l.with): Matthieu 23:6, Marc 12:39, Luc 14:7-8 20:46.†

G4414.def:
πρωτοστάτης, -ου, ὁ
(πρῶτος, ἵστημι) [in LXX: Job 15:24 AB * ;] 
prop., of soldiers, one who stands first, one in the front rank (Thuc., Xen.); hence, metaphorically, a leader: Actes 24:5.†

G4415.def:
πρωτοτόκια, -ων, τά
(πρωτότοκος) [in LXX (with seel. -εῖα, -εία): Genèse 25:31 ff. Genèse 27:36, Deutéronome 21:17, 1 Chroniques 5:1 (בְּכוֹרָה) * ;] 
the rights of the first-born, birthright (= cl. ἡ πρεσβεία): Hébreux 12:16.†

G4416.def:
πρωτότοκος, -ον
(πρῶτος, τίκτω) [in LXX chiefly for בְּכוֹר ;] 
first-born: Luc 2:7; pl., Hébreux 11:28. Metaphorical, of the priority of Christ (originally perh. a Messianic title, cf. Psaumes 89:28, Hébreux 1:6; see ICC on Colossiens 1:15): Hébreux 1:6; π. πάσης κτίσεως, Colossiens 1:15; ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς, Romains 8:29; π. (ἐκ) τ. νεκρῶν, Colossiens 1:18, Apocalypse 1:5; pl., of the elect, ἐκκλησία πρωτοτόκων, Hébreux 12:23.†

G4417.def:
πταίω 
[in LXX chiefly for נָגַף ni. ;] 
__1. trans., to cause to stumble (1 Rois 4:3, cf. Deiss., BS, 681). 
__2. Intrans., to stumble. Metaphorical, in moral sense, Romains 11:11, Jacques 2:10 3:2, 2 Pierre 1:10.†

G4418.def:
πτέρνα, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX for עָקֵב ;] 
the heel: figuratively, ἐπαίρειν τὴν π. ἐπί, Jean 13:18 (LXX).†

G4419.def:
πτερύγιον, -ου, -τό
(dimin. of πτέρυξ), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף ;] 
__1. a little wing. 
__2. Anything like a wing, as a turret, battlement: τ. ἱεροῦ, Matthieu 4:5, Luc 4:9.†

G4420.def:
πτέρυξ, -υγος, ἡ
(πέτομαι), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף ;] 
a wing: of birds, Matthieu 23:37, Luc 13:34, Apocalypse 12:14; of creatures seen in a vision, Apocalypse 4:8 9:9.†

G4421.def:
πτηνός, -ή, -όν
(πέτομαι), [in Aq.: Job 5:7 * ;] 
winged; as subst., π., birds: 1 Corinthiens 15:39.†

G4422.def:
πτοέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for חָתַת ni. ;] 
to terrify. Pass., to be terrified: Luc 21:9 24:37 (WH, mg., θροηθέντες).†

G4423.def:
πτόησις, -εως, ἡ
(πτοέω) [in LXX: Proverbes 3:25 (פַּחַד), Sir 50:4 א1, 1Ma.3:25 R * ;] 
a fluttering, excitement, caused by any emotion, but esp. by fear, hence, terror: φοβεῖσθαι πτόησιν, to be afraid with (cogn. accusative) or of any terror (see ICC, in l): 1 Pierre 3:6.†

G4424.def:
Πτολεμαΐς, -ΐδος, ἡ 
Ptolemais, a maritime city of Phœnicea: Actes 21:7.†

G4425.def:
πτύον, -ου, τό 
[in Sm.: Ésaïe 30:24 * ;] 
a winnowing shovel or fan: Matthieu 3:12, Luc 3:17.†

G4426.def:
πτύρομαι depon., 
to be startled, frightened: Philippiens 1:28. (The active πτύρω is also found in some late writers.) †

G4427.def:
πτύσμα, -τος, τό,
(πτύω) 
spittle: Jean 9:6 (Hipp., Polyb., al.).†

G4428.def:
πτύσσω 
to fold; of a scroll, to roll up: βιβλίον, Luc 4:20 (cf. ἀνα-πτύσσω).†

G4429.def:
πτύω 
[in LXX: Nombres 12:14 (יָרָק), Sir.28:12 * ;] 
to spit: Marc 7:33 8:23, Jean 9:6 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐμ-πτύω).†

G4431.def:
πτῶσις, -εως, ἡ
(πίπτω), [in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶף, מַפֶּלֶת, and cogn. forms ;] 
a falling, fall (Plat., Plut., al.): Matthieu 7:27; metaphorically, Luc 2:34.†

G4432.def:
πτωχεία, -ας, ἡ
(πτωχεύω), [in LXX chiefly for עֳנִי ;] 
beggary, destitution: 2 Corinthiens 8:2 8:9, Apocalypse 2:9.†

G4433.def:
πτωχεύω
(πτωχός), [in LXX: Juges 6:6, Psaumes 79:8 (דָּלַל); Juges 14:15 A, Proverbes 23:21 (יָרַשׁ); Psaumes 34:10 (רוּשׁ), Tob.4:21 * ;] 
__1. to be a beggar, to beg (so chiefly in cl.). 
__2. to be poor as a beggar, to be destitute, poor: opposite to πλούσιος ὤν, 2 Corinthiens 8:9.†

G4434.def:
πτωχός, -ή, -όν
(πτώσσω, to crouch, cower), [in LXX for עָנִי, דַּל, רָשׁ, etc. ;] 
of one who crouches and cowers, hence, 
__1. as subst., a beggar: Luc 14:13, 21 16:20, 22. 
__2. As adj., 
__(a) prop., beggarly: metaphorically, στοιχεῖα, Galates 4:9 (see Lft., in l); 
__(b) in broader sense (opposite to πλούσιος), poor: Matthieu 11:5 19:21 26:9, 11, Marc 10:21 12:42-43 14:5, 7, Luc 4:18 7:22 18:22 19:8 21:3, Jean 12:5-6, 8 13:29, Romains 15:26, 2 Corinthiens 6:10, Galates 2:10, Jacques 2:2-3, 6, Apocalypse 13:16; π. τ. κόσμῳ, Jacques 2:5; metaphorically, Luc 6:20, Apocalypse 3:17; π. τ. πνεύματι, Matthieu 5:3.†
SYN.: πένης, q.v

G4435.def:
πυγμή, -ῆς, ἡ 
[in LXX: Exode 21:18, Ésaïe 58:4 (אֶגְרֹף) * ;] 
the fist: πυγμῇ νίψασθαι τ. χῖρας (Τ, πυκνά; Vg., Goth., Copt., crebro), to wash the hands with the fist (diligently, R, txt.; up to the elbow, R, mg.; the exact meaning is doubtful; see Swete, in l): Marc 7:3.†

G4436.def:
πύθων, -ωνος, ὁ 
__1. in cl., Python, a serpent slain by Apollo, who is hence surnamed the Pythian. 
__2. In Plut. (ii, 414 E), a name given to ventriloquist soothsayers (ἐγγαστρίμυθοι; cf. Lévitique 19:31 20:6, 27, 1 Rois 28:7), and perhaps in this sense πνεῦμα πύθωνα, a python-spirit: Actes 16:16.†

G4437.def:
πυκιός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX: Eze.31:3 A (חֹרֶשׁ), 3Ma.1:28 3Mac 4:10, 4Ma.12:12 * ;] 
__1. close, compact, solid. 
__2. frequent: 1 Timothée 5:23. Neut. pl., πυκνά, as adv., much, often: Marc 7:3 Τ (see: πυγμή), Luc 5:33. Comparat., πυκνότερον, very often or so much the oftener (seeBl., § 44, 3,): Actes 24:26.†

G4438.def:
πυκτεύω
(πύκτης, a pugilist), 
to box: 1 Corinthiens 9:26.†

G4439.def:
πύλη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX chiefly and very frequently for שַׁעַר sometimes for דֶּלֶת, פֶּתַח ;] 
a gate: Luc 7:12, Actes 9:24 12:10 16:13, Hébreux 13:12; ἡ Ὡραία Π. τ. ἱεροῦ, Actes 3:10. Metaphorical, Matthieu 7:13-14; πύλαι ᾅδου (Wis.16:13, 3Ma.5:51, and cf. κλαῖς ᾅδου Apocalypse 1:18): Matthieu 16:18.†

G4440.def:
πυλών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(πύλη), [in LXX chiefly for פֶּתַח, שַׁעַר ;] 
__1. the porch or vestibule of a house or palace: Matthieu 26:71, Luc 16:20, Actes 10:17 12:13-14 
__2. The gate-way or gate-tower of a walled town: Actes 14:13, Apocalypse 21:12-13, 15 21:21, 25 22:14.†

G4441.def:
πυνθώ᾽ομαι 
[in LXX for דָּרַשׁ ;] 
__1. to inquire: with accusative of thing(s), Jean 4:42, Actes 23:20; before quæst. indir., Matthieu 2:4, Luc 15:25 18:36, Actes 10:18 21:33; quæst. dir., Actes 4:7 10:20 23:10; before παρά, with genitive of person(s), Matthieu 2:4, Jean 4:52. 
__2. to learn by inquiry: before ὅτι, Actes 23:34.†

G4442.def:
πῦρ genitive, πυρός, τό, 
[in LXX chiefly and very frequently for אֵשׁ ;] 
fire: Marc 9:22, Luc 3:9, Jean 15:6, Actes 2:10, 1 Corinthiens 3:13, Jacques 3:5, Apocalypse 8:5, al; π. καὶ θεῖον, Luc 17:29; κατακαίειν (ἐν) π., Matthieu 13:40, Apocalypse 17:16 18:8; καίεσθαι πυρί, Hébreux 12:18, Apocalypse 8:8 21:8; φλὸξ πυρός, Actes 7:30, 2 Thessaloniciens 1:8, Hébreux 1:7, Apocalypse 1:14 2:18 19:12; λαμπάδες πυρός, Apocalypse 4:5; στῦλοι πυρός, Apocalypse 10:1; ἄνθρακες πυρός, Romains 12:20 (LXX); γλῶσσαι ὡσεὶ πυρός, Actes 2:3; δοκιμάζειν (πυροῦσθαι) διὰ πυρός, 1 Pierre 1:7, Apocalypse 3:18; ὡς διὰ. π. (Lft., Notes, 193), 1 Corinthiens 3:15. Of the fire of hell (cf. Dalman, Words,161): Marc 9:48 (LXX); τὸ π. τὸ αἰώνιον, Matthieu 18:8 25:41 (cf. 4Ma.12:12); ἄσβεστον, Marc 9:43; πυρὸς αἰωνίου δίκην ὑπέχειν, Ju 7; γέεννα τοῦ π., Matthieu 5:22 18:9; κάμινος τοῦ π., Matthieu 13:42, 50; ἡ λίμνη τοῦ π., Apocalypse 19:20 20:10, 14-15; πυρὶ τηρεῖσθαι, 2 Pierre 3:7; βασανισθῆναι ἐν π., Apocalypse 14:10. Metaphorical: βαπτίζειν πυρί, Luc 3:16; of the tongue, Jacques 3:5; of strife and discord, Luc 12:49; ἐκ π. ἁρπάζειν, Ju 23; πυρὶ αλίζεσθαι, Marc 9:49; ζῆλος πυρός, Hébreux 10:27; of God, π, καταναλίσκον, Hébreux 12:29 (LXX)

G4443.def:
πυρά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
(πῦρ) [in LXX: Jdth.7:5, Wis.17:6, al. ;] 
a fire: Actes 28:2-3.†

G4444.def:
πύργος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for מִגְדָּל ;] 
a tower: Luc 13:4; of a watch-tower in a vineyard (Ésaïe 5:2): Matthieu 21:33, Marc 12:1, and prob., Luc 14:28.†

G4445.def:
πυρέσσω 
(πῦρ) 
to be ill of a fever: Matthieu 8:14, Marc 1:3.†

G4446.def:
πυρετός, -οῦ, ὁ 
(πῦρ) [in LXX: Deutéronome 28:22 (קַדַּחַת) * ;] 
a fever: Matthieu 8:15, Marc 1:31, Luc 4:39, Jean 4:52, Actes 28:8; π. μέγας, a high fever: Luc 4:38 (on the technical phrase here, see MM, xxii).†

G4447.def:
πύρινος, -η, -ον 
[in LXX: Eze.28:14, 16 (אֵשׁ), Sir.48:9 * ;] 
fiery: Apocalypse 9:17.†

G4448.def:
πυρόω, -ῶ 
(πῦρ) [in LXX chiefly for צָרַף ;] 
to set on fire, burn up. In NT always pass., 
__1. to be set on fire, to burn: Éphésiens 6:16, 2 Pierre 3:12; ptcp., glowing, Apocalypse 1:15. Metaphorical, of grief or indignation, 2 Corinthiens 11:29; of lust, 1 Corinthiens 7:9. 
__2. Of metals (cf. Job 22:25, Psaumes 12:7, Zacharie 13:9), to be refined or purified by fire: Apocalypse 3:18 (and so in RV, Apocalypse 1:15, but see supr.).†

G4449.def:
πυρράζω
(πυρρός), [in LXX, πυρρίζω: Lévitique 13:19, 42 ff. Lévitique 14:37 (אֲדַמְדָּם) * ;] 
to be fiery red: Matthieu 16:2-3.†

G4450.def:
πυρρός -ά, -όν 
(πῦρ) [in LXX for אֱדֹם ;] 
fiery red: Apocalypse 6:4 12:3.† 
Πύρρος, -ου, ὁ, 
Pyrrhus: Actes 20:4.†

G4451.def:
πύρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(πυρόω), [in LXX: Proverbes 27:21 (כּוּר), Amos 4:9 (שְׁדֵפָה) * ;] 
__1. a burning: Apocalypse 18:9, 18. 
__2. a refining or trial by fire: metaphorically, 1 Pierre 4:12.†

G4453.def:
πωλέω, -ῶ 
[in LXX chiefly for מָכַר ;] 
__1. to exchange or barter. 
__2. to sell: Luc 17:28, Apocalypse 13:17; οἱ πωλοῦντες, Matthieu 21:12 25:9, Marc 11:15, Luc 19:45; with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 13:44 19:21 21:12, Marc 10:21 11:15, Luc 12:33 18:22 22:36, Jean 2:14, 16 Actes 5:1 (sc. αὐτά, αὐτόν), Actes 4:34, 37. Pass., 1 Corinthiens 10:25; with genitive pretii, Matthieu 10:29, Luc 12:6.†

G4454.def:
πῶλος, -ου, ὁ
(in cl. also ) [in LXX chiefly for עַיִר ;] 
a foal, colt, prop., of a horse, then the young of other animals; in NT of the colt of an ass: Matthieu 21:2, 5" (LXX), Matthieu 21:7, Marc 11:2, 4-5 11:7, Luc 19:30, 33 19:35, Jean 12:15" (LXX) .†

G4455.def:
πώ-ποτε 
adv., 
ever yet: Luc 19:30, Jean 1:18 5:37 6:35 8:33, 1 Jean 4:12.†

G4456.def:
πωρόω, -ῶ
(πῶρος, 1. a stone. 2. a callus) [in LXX: Job 17:7 B(כָּהָה), Proverbes 10:20 A * ;] 
to petrify, harden, form a callus. Metaphorical, π. τ. καρδίαν, Jean 12:40. Pass., Romains 11:7; τ. νοήματα, 2 Corinthiens 3:14; ἡ καρδία, Marc 6:52 8:17 †

G4457.def:
πώρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(πωρόω), 
a covering with a callus, a hardening: metaphorically, Marc 3:6, Romains 11:2, Éphésiens 4:18.†

G4458.def:
πως, 
enclit. part., 
at all; see: εἴπως, μήπως. 
μήπως
or μή πως (so WH), 
negative particle, 
__1. as conjc., lest haply: in final sentences, 1 Corinthiens 9:27, 2 Corinthiens 2:7 9:4; after verbs of fearing or taking heed, 1 Corinthiens 8:9, 2 Corinthiens 11:3 12:20, Galates 4:11; with an ellipse of ptcp. (sc. φοβούμενος; cf. B1., § 65, 3; Burton, § 225), 1 Thessaloniciens 3:5 (but see infr.). 
__2. As interrogative, whether haply: Galates 2:2, 1 Thessaloniciens 3:5 (cf. M, Th., in l, but see supr.).†
μήπου
(WH, μή που), 
lest anywhere, lest haply: Actes 27:29.†

G4459.def:
πῶς, interrog. adv., correl. of ὅπως, 
__1. prop., in direct questions, how?: with indic., Matthieu 12:29, Marc 3:23, Luc 11:18, Jean 3:4, al.; καὶ π., Marc 4:13, Luc 20:44; π. οὖν, Matthieu 12:26; π. οὐ, Matthieu 16:11, Luc 12:56; in deliberative questions (cf. Bl., §64, 6), with subjc., Matthieu 23:33 26:54; π. οὖν, Romains 10:14; π. δέ, Romains 10:14, 15; before ἄν, with optative, Actes 8:31. 
__2. As sometimes in cl. but more frequently and increasingly so in late writers (see WM, §57, 2; Bl., §70, 2; Thumb, MGr., 192; Jannaris, Gr., App., vi, 13f.), = ὅπως, ὥς; 
__(a) in indirect discourse: with indic., Matthieu 6:28, Marc 12:41, Luc 8:36, Jean 9:15, Actes 9:27, al.; with subjc., Marc 11:18, Luc 12:11; 
__(b) in exclamations: Matthieu 21:20, Marc 10:23, 24 Luc 12:50 18:24, Jean 11:36.

G4460.def:
Ῥαάβ
(and Ραχάβ, Matthieu 1:5; Ραχάβη, -ης, in FlJ), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. רָחָב) 
Rahab (LXX, Josué 2:1, al.): Hébreux 11:31, Jacques 2:25.†

G4461.def:
ῥαββεί (Rec. -βί, see WH, App., 155) (Heb. and Aram. רַב, my master; see Dalman, Words, 327, 331 ff.), 
a title of respectful address to Jewish teachers, Rabbi: Matthieu 23:7-8; of John, Jean 3:26; of Christ, Matthieu 26:25, 49, Marc 9:5 11:21 14:45, Jean 1:30, 50 3:2 4:31 6:25 9:2 11:8; κύριε ῥ Marc 10:51 (WH, mg., see: ῥαββουνεί).†
ῥαββουνεί (Rec. -βονί, see: ῥαββεί) (Aram. רַבּוֺנִי, later, רִבּוֺנִי my master; on the Greek vocalization and the relation of the word to ῥαββεί, see Dalman, Words, 324, 340; Gr., 140; DB, iv, 190) 
Rabboni: Marc 10:51 (WH, mg., κύριε ῥαββεί), Jean 20:16.†

G4462.def:
ῥαββουνεί (Rec. -βονί, see: ῥαββεί) (Aram. רַבּוֺנִי, later, רִבּוֺנִי my master; on the Greek vocalization and the relation of the word to ῥαββεί, see Dalman, Words, 324, 340; Gr., 140; DB, iv, 190) 
Rabboni: Marc 10:51 (WH, mg., κύριε ῥαββεί), Jean 20:16.†

G4463.def:
ῥαβδίζω
(ῥάβδος), [in LXX: Juges 6:11 Ruth 2:17 (חָבַט) * ;] 
to beat with a rod: Actes 16:22, 2 Corinthiens 11:25.†

G4466.def:
Ῥαγαύ (Rec. -αῦ), ὁ, indecl. (LXX for Heb. רְעוּ, Genèse 11:18, al.), 
Reu: Luc 3:35.†

G4467.def:
ῥᾳδιούργημα, -τος, τό
(ῥᾳδιουργέω, to act recklessly or wrongly) 
__1. a reckless act. 
__2. crime, villany: Actes 18:14.†

G4468.def:
ῥᾳδιουργία, -ας, ἡ
(see: ῥᾳδιούργημα), 
__1. ease in doing, facility (Xen.). 
__2. easiness, laziness (Xen.). 
__3. recklessness, wickedness (of lewdness, Xen.; fraud, Plut.; in π., of theft, MM, xxii): Actes 13:10.†

G4469.def:
ῥακά (T, ῥαχά), 
usually taken to represent the Aram. רֵיקָא, a shortened form of H7386, " empty," as vocalized in the Galilæan dialect; an expression of contempt, raca: Matthieu 5:22 (cf. DB, iv, 191 f.; and for other explanations, see Zorell, see word).†

G4470.def:
ῥάκος, -ους, τό 
[in LXX: Ésaïe 64:6 (5) (בֶּגֶד), Jérémie 38:11 (סְחָבָה), Esther 4:17 * ;] 
__1. a ragged garment (Hom.). 
__2. a rag, remnant, piece of cloth: Matthieu 9:16, Marc 2:21.†

G4471.def:
Ῥαμά (Rec. -ᾶ), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. רָמָה), 
Ramah: Matthieu 2:18 (LXX).†

G4472.def:
ῥαντίζω 
[in LXX: Lévitique 6:27 (20), 4Ki.9:33 (נָזָה), Psaumes 51:7 (חָטָא pi.) * ;] 
= cl., ῥαίνω, 
to sprinkle, besprinkle: with accusative, Hébreux 9:13, 19; id. and dative, Hébreux 9:21; pass., Apocalypse 19:13, WH; of cleansing by sprinkling, Hébreux 10:22 (see M, Gr., ii, 100); mid., Marc 7:4 (WH, txt., R, mg.).†
περι-ραίνω 
(-ρραίνω, Rec., see WH, App., 139 f.), [in LXX for נָזָה hi. ;] 
to sprinkle around: Apocalypse 19:13 T (ῤεραντισμένον, WH; ῤε-, R, txt.; βεβαμμένον, Rec., R, mg.).†

G4473.def:
ῥαντισμός, -ῦo, ὁ
(ῥαντίζω), [in LXX for נִדָּה ;] 
sprinkling: of the ceremonial sprinkling of blood for purification, Hébreux 12:24, 1 Pierre 1:2 (see Hort, Pe., 23 ff.).†

G4474.def:
ῥαπίζω
(ῥαπίς, a rod), [in LXX: Juges 16:25, Hébreux 11:4, I Esther 4:11 * ;] 
__1. prop., to strike with a rod. 
__2. In late writers, to strike (the face) with the palm of the hand: Matthieu 26:67; with accusative of person(s), before εἰς τ. σιαγόνα, Matthieu 5:39 (cf. Field, Notes, 40, 105).†

G4475.def: a stroke, a slap on the face , (Lucian) (ML)

G4476.def:
ῥαφίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(ῥάπτω, to sew), 
a needle: Matthieu 19:24, Marc 10:25 (cf. βελόνη).†

G4477.def:
A woman living before Israel's Monarchy, first mentioned at Josué 2:1; 
mother of: Boaz (H1162)(?) 
§ Rahab, "spacious, broad" 
Rachab, (Proper name), indeclinable, Mt. 1:5*

G4478.def:
Ῥαχήλ, ἡ indecl. (Heb. רָחֵל), 
Rachel: Matthieu 2:18 (LXX).†

G4479.def:
Ῥεβέκκα, -ας (see Bl., § 7, 2), ἡ, (Heb. רִבְקָה), 
Rebecca: Romains 9:10.†

G4480.def:
ῥέδη (see WH, App., 151), -ης, ἡ 
(a Gallic word), 
a chariot: Apocalypse 18:13.†

G4481.def:
Ῥεμφάν, Ῥεφάς, see: Ῥομφά.
Ῥομφά (-άν, T; Ῥεφάν, LTr.; Ῥεμφάν, Rec.; see WH, App., 92), 
[in LXX: Amos 5:26 (Ῥαιμφάν or Ῥεφάν, Heb. כִּיּוּן)* ;] 
Rompha, Rephan (RV), one of the names of Seb, the Egyptian Saturn: Actes 7:43 (LXX).†

G4482.def:
ῥέω 
[in LXX chiefly for זוּב ;] 
to flow: Jean 7:38 (cf. παραρρέω).†

G4483.def:
λέγω, 
[in LXX very freq., chiefly for אמר; λέγει for נְאֻם, Genèse 22:16, al. ;] 
__1. in Hom., to pick out, gather, reckon, recount.
__2. In Hdt. and Att., to say, speak, affirm, declare: absol., Actes 13:15, 24:10; before orat. dir., Matthieu 9:34, Marc 3:11, Jean 1:29, al.; before ὅτι recit., Marc 3:21, Luc 1:24, Jean 6:14, al.; accusative and inf., Luc 11:18, Jean 12:29, al.; after another verb of speaking, προσφωνεῖν κ. λέγειν, Matthieu 11:17, al.; ἀπεκρίθη (ἐλάλησεν) λέγων (καὶ λέγει; Dalman, Words, 24 ff.), Matthieu 25:9, Marc 3:33, 7:28, Luc 24:6, 7, al.; of unspoken thought, λ. ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Matthieu 3:9, Luc 3:8, al.; of writing, 2 Corinthiens 8:8, Philippiens 4:11, al.; λέγει ἡ γραφή, Romains 4:3, Jacques 2:23, al.; with accusative of thing(s), Luc 8:8, 9:33, Jean 5:34, al.; σὺ λέγεις (a non-committal phrase; Swete, Mk., 359, 369f.), Matthieu 27:11, Marc 15:2, Luc 23:3, Jean 18:37; with dative of person(s), before orat. dir., Matthieu 8:20, Marc 2:17, al. mult.; id. before ὅτι, Matthieu 3:9, al.; with prep., πρός, μετά, περί, etc., Marc 4:41, Jean 11:56, Hébreux 9:5, al.; to mean (cl.), Marc 14:71, Jean 6:71, 1 Corinthiens 10:29, al.; to call, name, Marc 10:18; pass., Matthieu 9:9, Marc 15:7, al (cf. ἀντι-, δια- (-μαι), προ-, συλ-λέγω). 
SYN.: λαλέω, which refers to the utterance, as λέγω to the meaning of what is said, its correspondence with thought (Tr., Syn., Ixxvi; Thayer, see word λαλέω).

G4484.def:
Ῥήγιον, -ου, τό 
Rhegium, a town in Sicily: Actes 28:13.†

G4485.def:
ῥῆγμα, -τος, τό
(ῥήγνυμι), [in LXX: 3Ki.11:30-31 12:24, 4Ki.2:12 (קֶרַע), Amos 6:12 (11) A (בְּקִיעַ) * ;] 
__1. cl. (and so in LXX), a fracture; then by meton., that which is torn. 
__2. In NT, ruin: Luc 6:49.†

G4486.def:
ῥήγνυμι and (Marc 9:18) ῥήσσω, 
[in LXX chiefly for בָּקַע, also for קָרַע, etc. ;] 
__1. to rend, break asunder: Matthieu 7:6, Marc 2:22, Luc 5:37; pass., Matthieu 9:17. 
__2. Of the voice, with accusative, φωνήν, etc. (Hdt., al.), to break forth into speech: absol., Galates 4:27 (LXX). 
__3. = ῥήσσω (Dem., al.), to throw or dash down: Marc 9:18, Luc 9:42 
(cf. δια-, περι-, προσ-ρήγνυμι).†
SYN.: θραύω, κατάγνυμι

G4487.def:
ῥῆμα, -τος, τό 
[in LXX chiefly for דָּבָר, also for פֶּה, and Aram. פִּתְגָּם, etc. ;] 
__1. prop., of that which is said or spoken, 
__(a) a word: Matthieu 27:14, 2 Corinthiens 12:4; pl., τὰ ῥ., of speech, discourse, Luc 7:1, Jean 8:20, Actes 2:14, Romains 10:18, 2 Pierre 3:2, al.; 
__(b) opposite to ὄνομα (a single word), a saying, statement, word of prophecy, instruction or command (in cl., phrase): Matthieu 26:75, Marc 9:32, Luc 1:38 2:50, Actes 11:16, Romains 10:8, Hébreux 11:3; ῥ. θεοῦ (κυρίου), Luc 3:2, Actes 11:16, Éphésiens 6:17, Hébreux 6:5 11:3, 1 Pierre 1:25" (LXX) ; τὰ ῥ. τ. θεοῦ, Jean 3:34 8:47; ῥ. ἀργόν, Matthieu 12:36;ῥ. ἄρρητα, 2 Corinthiens 12:4. 
__2. Like Heb. דָּבָר (but perh. also a Gk. colloquialism, see Kennedy, Sources, 124; Thackeray, Gr., 41), of that which is the subject of speech, a thing, matter (Genèse 15:1, Deutéronome 17:8, al.): Luc 1:37 2:15, Actes 10:37; pl., Luc 1:65 2:19, 51, Actes 5:32 13:42

G4489.def:
ῥήτωρ, -ορος, ὁ 
a public speaker, an orator: Actes 24:1.†

G4490.def:
ῥητῶς 
adv. (ῥητός, stated, specified), 
in stated terms, expressly: 1 Timothée 4:1.†

G4492.def:
ῥιζόω, -ῶ
(ῥίζα), [in LXX: Ésaïe 40:24, Jérémie 12:2 (שָׁרַשׁ), Sir.3:28 24:12 * ;] 
to cause to take root. Metaphorical, to plant, fix firmly, establish: pass. (EV, rooted), ἐν ἀγάπῃ, Éphésiens 3:18(17); ἐν Χριστῷ, Colossiens 2:7 (cf. ἐκ ριζόω).†

G4493.def:
ῥιπή, ῆς, ἡ
(ῥίπτω), 
poët. in cl., any rapid movement such as the throw or flight of a javelin, the rush of wind or flame, the flapping of wings, the twinkling of lights; ῥ. ὀφθαλμοῦ, the twinkling of an eye: 1 Corinthiens 15:52 (L, mg., ῥοπή, which see).†

G4494.def:
ῥιπίζω
(ῥιπίς, a fan) [in LXX: Dan LXX 2:35 (נְשָׂא) * ;] 
primarily, to fan a fire, hence generally, to make a breeze (Plut., al.). In pass. (cf. Philo, de inter. round., 24), to be tossed or blown by the wind: of waves, ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ, blown and raised with the wind (Hort, in l), Jacques 1:6.†

G4496.def:
ῥίπτω and (Actes 22:23) ῥιπτέω (strengthened form; see Veitch, see word ῥίπτω, fin.), 
[in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַךְ hi. ;] 
__1. to throw, cast, hurl: with accusative of thing(s), Matthieu 27:5, Actes 27:19, 29; with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 15:30, Luc 4:35; pass., Luc 17:2; ptcp., ἐριμμένοι, cast down, prostrate (Polyb., al.): Matthieu 9:36; of garments, to throw off (for flight, Eur., Xen., al.; ὅπλα, 1Ma.5:43; so EV in Actes 22:23, but see infr.). 
__2. = ῥιπτάζω, to shake, toss, throw about: τ. ἱμάτια, Actes 22:23 (EGT, Page, Rackham, in l; Field, Notes, 136; but see supr.).†

G4497.def:
Ῥοβοάμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. רְחַבְעָם), 
Rehoboam: Matthieu 1:7.†

G4499.def: the isle of Rhodes , (Iliad by Homer), etc. (ML)
